S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

symptom.disease_info: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder is characterized by intrusive, unwanted obsessions and repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed to reduce distress or prevent feared outcomes, with the pattern becoming time-consuming or functionally impairing. It often has a fluctuating course and is distinguished from ordinary worry, perfectionism, or habits by the ego-dystonic quality of the thoughts and the excessive, rigid, or not realistically connected nature of the compulsions.

patient.stressor_event: Taking on a mortgage (for home, business)
patient.stressor: After her divorce, Nina bought a small Visalia bungalow with a garden and a spare room she planned to use as a design studio, taking on a mortgage that made every client invoice and household decision feel more consequential. What began as careful reviewing of loan papers, client proofs, and home expenses gradually became a pattern of intrusive, unwanted doubts followed by repeated checking and mental reviewing that she could not easily set aside. Over an unclear period, the rituals began cutting into billable design hours, delaying community-project deadlines, and making even quiet evenings in the garden feel governed by unfinished verification. She eventually contacted a psychiatrist herself after a longtime client questioned why a simple logo revision had taken weeks despite her usual organized workflow.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: What brings me in is that I keep getting these awful doubts that I've missed something important—a number on the mortgage payment, a clause in a client proof, a door not latched—and even when I know I checked it, the thought barges back in like, 'What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?'

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: I end up reopening files, rereading emails, checking the online payment confirmation, and sometimes saying the figures silently in my head until they feel 'settled,' which can turn a simple invoice or logo revision into hours I can't bill for.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve missed billable hours and pushed back deadlines because work that used to take an afternoon now drags on for days, and one longtime client has already questioned whether I can still handle simple revisions on time.
